Cell Biology.mechanism: osmotic water movement across the semipermeable plasma membrane
Cell Biology.conceptNote: Water moves osmotically from regions of lower solute concentration to higher solute concentration, so cells swell in hypotonic media and shrink in hypertonic media.

Molecular Biology.mechanism: inducer binding releases the repressor from the operator to permit RNA polymerase transcription
Molecular Biology.conceptNote: Gene expression is controlled at the level of transcription, where inducers can inactivate repressor proteins and allow RNA polymerase to bind the promoter.

Genetics.mechanism: Mendelian segregation and independent assortment of alleles during gamete formation
Genetics.conceptNote: A monohybrid cross between two heterozygotes (Aa x Aa) yields a 3:1 dominant-to-recessive phenotypic ratio because alleles segregate independently into gametes.

Cardiovascular System.mechanism: Frank-Starling stretch-dependent increase in myocardial contractile force
Cardiovascular System.conceptNote: By the Frank-Starling mechanism, increased ventricular filling stretches cardiac muscle fibers and raises stroke volume, so cardiac output rises with venous return.

Respiratory System.mechanism: cooperative binding of O2 to the four heme subunits of hemoglobin
Respiratory System.conceptNote: The oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve is sigmoidal because cooperative binding makes each successive O2 molecule bind hemoglobin more readily.

Renal System.mechanism: myogenic and tubuloglomerular feedback autoregulation of glomerular capillary pressure
Renal System.conceptNote: Renal autoregulation holds glomerular filtration rate nearly constant over a wide range of arterial pressures by adjusting afferent arteriole resistance.

Digestive System.mechanism: pH-dependent activation and denaturation of digestive proteases such as pepsin
Digestive System.conceptNote: Each digestive enzyme has an optimal pH; pepsin is most active in the acidic stomach (pH 2), while trypsin works best in the alkaline small intestine.

Nervous System.mechanism: voltage-gated sodium channel activation once membrane potential reaches threshold
Nervous System.conceptNote: Action potentials are all-or-none, so stronger stimuli are encoded not by larger spikes but by an increased frequency of firing above threshold.

Endocrine System.mechanism: insulin receptor signaling drives GLUT4 translocation and cellular glucose uptake
Endocrine System.conceptNote: Insulin lowers blood glucose by binding its receptor and promoting GLUT4-mediated glucose uptake into muscle and adipose tissue.

Immune System.mechanism: memory B-cell clonal expansion and affinity maturation upon repeat antigen exposure
Immune System.conceptNote: The secondary immune response produces a faster, larger, higher-affinity antibody titer than the primary response because of immunological memory B cells.

Reproductive System.mechanism: estrogen-triggered positive feedback driving the mid-cycle LH surge that ruptures the follicle
Reproductive System.conceptNote: A mid-cycle surge of luteinizing hormone, triggered by peak estrogen via positive feedback, induces ovulation by rupturing the mature ovarian follicle.

Microbiology.mechanism: exponential binary fission during the log phase of bacterial growth
Microbiology.conceptNote: Bacteria multiply by binary fission, producing exponential (logarithmic) growth during the log phase before nutrient limits force a stationary phase.

Evolution.mechanism: natural selection enriching pre-existing resistance alleles under directional selection
Evolution.conceptNote: Natural selection increases the frequency of advantageous alleles over generations, as antibiotic exposure favors survival and reproduction of resistant variants.

Atomic Structure.mechanism: increasing effective nuclear charge with constant shielding
Atomic Structure.conceptNote: First ionization energy generally rises across a period because effective nuclear charge increases while electrons enter the same principal shell, pulling them more tightly.

Chemical Bonding.mechanism: increased orbital overlap and shared electron density between nuclei
Chemical Bonding.conceptNote: Higher bond order means more shared electron pairs and greater orbital overlap, which shortens the bond and raises the energy required to break it.

Stoichiometry.mechanism: fixed mole ratios fixed by the balanced chemical equation
Stoichiometry.conceptNote: Product yield is fixed by the limiting reactant through the balanced equation's mole ratios; once one reactant is exhausted, adding more of the other yields no additional product.

Thermodynamics.mechanism: the entropy term TdeltaS increasingly offsetting enthalpy in deltaG = deltaH - TdeltaS
Thermodynamics.conceptNote: Spontaneity is governed by deltaG = deltaH - TdeltaS, so for an endothermic, entropy-increasing reaction raising temperature makes deltaG more negative and the process spontaneous.

Chemical Kinetics.mechanism: collision frequency and activation energy thresholds
Chemical Kinetics.conceptNote: Rate increases with reactant concentration because more frequent molecular collisions raise the number of successful collisions exceeding the activation energy per unit time.

Equilibrium.mechanism: Le Chatelier shift toward the side with fewer gas moles
Equilibrium.conceptNote: By Le Chatelier's principle, increasing pressure on a gas-phase equilibrium shifts the position toward the side with fewer moles of gas, raising the yield when products occupy less volume.

Acids and Bases.independentVariable: volume of strong base titrant added
Acids and Bases.mechanism: neutralization and buffering near the conjugate acid pKa
Acids and Bases.conceptNote: During titration of a weak acid, pH equals the pKa at the half-equivalence point and rises sharply at the equivalence point where moles of added base equal the initial moles of acid.

Electrochemistry.independentVariable: ratio of ion concentrations at the electrodes
Electrochemistry.mechanism: Nernst-equation dependence of potential on reaction quotient
Electrochemistry.conceptNote: The Nernst equation, E = E0 - (RT/nF)lnQ, shows that cell potential decreases logarithmically as the reaction quotient rises toward equilibrium where E reaches zero.

Solutions.mechanism: colligative disruption of solvent crystal lattice formation by dissolved particles
Solutions.conceptNote: Freezing point depression is a colligative property given by deltaTf = i*Kf*m, depending only on the molal concentration of dissolved particles and the van't Hoff factor, not their identity.

Functional Groups.conceptNote: Each functional group absorbs infrared light at a characteristic wavenumber set by the bond's stiffness and the reduced mass of its atoms, so a carbonyl appears near 1715 cm-1 and an O-H or N-H stretch appears as a broad band near 3300 cm-1.

Nomenclature.conceptNote: IUPAC nomenclature names a compound by selecting the longest carbon chain containing the highest-priority functional group as the parent and numbering it to give that group and the substituents the lowest set of locants.

Organic Reactions.conceptNote: In a bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) the rate and product yield depend on the concentration of both the nucleophile and the substrate, because the rate-determining step is a single concerted collision between them.

Reaction Mechanisms.conceptNote: In an SN1 or E1 mechanism the slow step is ionization to form a carbocation, so reactivity rises sharply as the leaving group becomes a weaker base (the conjugate acid has a lower pKa) and can stabilize the departing electron pair.

Stereochemistry.conceptNote: A solution's measured optical rotation is directly proportional to its enantiomeric excess, so a racemic 50:50 mixture is optically inactive while an enantiopure sample gives the full specific rotation of that enantiomer.

Amino Acids.mechanism: sequential proton dissociation at characteristic pKa values
Amino Acids.conceptNote: An amino acid carries no net charge at its isoelectric point, where the zwitterion predominates and positive and negative charges balance.

Enzymes.conceptNote: Enzyme velocity rises hyperbolically with substrate concentration toward Vmax, with Km equal to the substrate concentration giving half-maximal rate.

Metabolism.outcome: glycolytic flux measured as lactate production
Metabolism.mechanism: allosteric activation of phosphofructokinase-1 at the committed step
Metabolism.conceptNote: Phosphofructokinase-1 catalyzes the committed, rate-limiting step of glycolysis and is allosterically activated by fructose-2,6-bisphosphate and AMP.

Bioenergetics.outcome: ATP synthesis rate by oxidative phosphorylation
Bioenergetics.independentVariable: proton-motive force across the inner membrane
Bioenergetics.mechanism: chemiosmotic coupling driving ATP synthase rotation
Bioenergetics.conceptNote: ATP synthesis is driven by the proton-motive force established by the electron transport chain, coupling proton flow through ATP synthase to phosphorylation.

Protein Structure.outcome: fraction of protein in folded native state
Protein Structure.mechanism: disruption of noncovalent stabilizing interactions causing cooperative unfolding
Protein Structure.conceptNote: Protein tertiary structure is stabilized by hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions, and disulfide bonds, and chemical denaturants unfold proteins in a cooperative transition.

Carbohydrates.mechanism: temperature-dependent cleavage of alpha-1,4 glycosidic bonds with enzyme denaturation at high heat
Carbohydrates.conceptNote: Amylase hydrolyzes alpha-1,4 glycosidic bonds in starch, and its activity peaks near physiological temperature before declining as the enzyme denatures.

Lipids.mechanism: cholesterol intercalation modulating phospholipid acyl-chain packing
Lipids.conceptNote: Cholesterol buffers membrane fluidity by restraining fluidity above the phase-transition temperature while preventing tight packing below it.

Nucleic Acids.mechanism: thermal disruption of complementary base-pair hydrogen bonds
Nucleic Acids.conceptNote: DNA melting temperature rises with GC content because guanine-cytosine pairs form three hydrogen bonds versus two for adenine-thymine.

Kinematics.mechanism: decomposition of initial velocity into independent horizontal and vertical components
Kinematics.conceptNote: For projectile motion at fixed speed, range follows R = v squared sin(2 theta) divided by g, peaking at a 45 degree launch angle.

Dynamics.mechanism: Newton's second law relating net force, mass, and acceleration
Dynamics.conceptNote: By Newton's second law a = F_net / m, acceleration is directly proportional to net force for a fixed mass, giving a straight line through the origin.

Work and Energy.mechanism: conversion of kinetic energy into elastic potential energy stored in the spring
Work and Energy.conceptNote: By conservation of energy, a block's kinetic energy converts to spring potential energy 0.5 k x squared, so compression scales with the square root of input energy.

Momentum.outcome: post-collision velocity of the struck cart
Momentum.independentVariable: incoming velocity of the striking cart
Momentum.mechanism: conservation of linear momentum in an elastic collision between equal masses
Momentum.conceptNote: In a one-dimensional elastic collision between equal masses, the moving cart stops and transfers its entire velocity to the stationary cart by conservation of momentum and kinetic energy.

Fluids.outcome: volumetric flow rate through a pipe
Fluids.mechanism: viscous laminar flow governed by the Hagen-Poiseuille relationship
Fluids.conceptNote: For laminar flow, Poiseuille's law makes volumetric flow rate directly proportional to the pressure gradient and to the fourth power of the tube radius.

Waves and Sound.outcome: fundamental frequency of a vibrating string
Waves and Sound.mechanism: dependence of wave speed on tension and linear mass density in a standing wave
Waves and Sound.conceptNote: For a string of fixed length, the fundamental frequency is proportional to the square root of tension, since wave speed equals the square root of tension over linear mass density.

Optics.outcome: image distance from a converging lens
Optics.mechanism: refraction described by the thin-lens equation relating object and image distances to focal length
Optics.conceptNote: The thin-lens equation 1/f = 1/d_o + 1/d_i shows image distance rises sharply as the object approaches the focal point and diverges to infinity at f.

Electrostatics.mechanism: Coulomb's inverse-square law of electrostatic attraction or repulsion
Electrostatics.conceptNote: By Coulomb's law, the force between two point charges is proportional to the product of their charges and inversely proportional to the square of their separation.

Circuits.mechanism: Ohmic conduction relating current, voltage, and resistance
Circuits.conceptNote: For an ohmic resistor at constant resistance, Ohm's law I = V/R makes current directly proportional to applied voltage, giving a straight line through the origin.

Magnetism.outcome: magnetic force on a current-carrying wire
Magnetism.independentVariable: current through the wire in a fixed field
Magnetism.mechanism: the magnetic Lorentz force on moving charge given by F = B I L sin theta
Magnetism.conceptNote: The force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is F = B I L sin theta, so for fixed field, length, and angle the force is directly proportional to current.

Thermodynamics.outcome: final equilibrium temperature change of water
Thermodynamics.mechanism: specific heat capacity relating absorbed heat to temperature rise via Q = m c delta T
Thermodynamics.conceptNote: By Q = m c delta T, the temperature rise of a fixed mass of substance is directly proportional to the heat added and inversely proportional to its specific heat capacity.

Sensation, Perception.mechanism: sensory transduction and signal-detection above absolute threshold
Sensation, Perception.conceptNote: The absolute threshold is the minimum stimulus intensity detectable 50 percent of the time, and detection probability rises sigmoidally as intensity increases.

Learning & Memory.mechanism: associative strengthening of the CS-US link via classical conditioning
Learning & Memory.conceptNote: In classical conditioning, repeated pairing of a conditioned stimulus with an unconditioned stimulus produces a learning curve where conditioned-response strength grows with trials toward asymptote.

Cognition, Consciousness, Language.mechanism: automatic word reading interfering with controlled color naming in selective attention
Cognition, Consciousness, Language.conceptNote: The Stroop effect shows that automatic processing of word meaning interferes with the controlled task of naming ink color, slowing response time most in the incongruent condition.

Emotion, Stress, Identity.mechanism: HPA-axis activation releasing cortisol in response to perceived threat
Emotion, Stress, Identity.conceptNote: Acute psychosocial stress activates the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, increasing cortisol secretion in proportion to the appraised intensity of the stressor.

Social Processes I - Self & Others.mechanism: normative social influence increasing with majority group size
Social Processes I - Self & Others.conceptNote: In Asch-style conformity studies, the tendency to agree with an incorrect majority rises sharply as group size grows to about three or four and then plateaus.

Social Processes II - Groups, Culture &.mechanism: diffusion of responsibility reducing individual helping in larger groups
Social Processes II - Groups, Culture &.conceptNote: The bystander effect shows that the likelihood any individual intervenes in an emergency decreases as the number of bystanders increases, due to diffusion of responsibility.

Social Inequality & Health.mechanism: social gradient in health from differential access to resources and chronic stress
Social Inequality & Health.conceptNote: The social gradient in health describes a stepwise rise in morbidity and mortality as socioeconomic status declines, driven by unequal access to resources and greater chronic-stress exposure.

Biological Bases of Behaviour.mechanism: mesolimbic dopamine signaling in the reward pathway driving reinforcement
Biological Bases of Behaviour.conceptNote: Mesolimbic dopamine activity in the nucleus accumbens mediates reward and reinforcement, so dopaminergic stimulation dose-dependently increases reward-seeking operant behavior.
